newsitem.title: UK: US Drug agent wins damages over Lockerbie film.
newsitem.headline: US Drug agent wins damages over Lockerbie film.

text.p: A retired U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) agent on Wednesday accepted 17,500 pounds ($29,060) in damages after he claimed a television programme linked his name to the 1988 Lockerbie bombing.
Michael Hurley, who worked with the U.S embassy in Nicosia, Cyprus, took Channel Four television to court over the May 1995 programme which he said implicated him in the bombing.
His lawyer told the court that the film alleged a passenger on the plane was a DEA courier and informant and that his bag, containing drugs, was switched by bombers without his knowledge.

"Some viewers of the film may have wrongly concluded that because Mr Hurley was head of the DEA Cyprus office at the time, the film was claiming that Pan Am Flight 103 had been blown up due to some negligence of his," defence lawyer William Bennett said.
Channel Four apologised and agreed to pay Hurley's costs as well as the agreed damages.
The United States alleges that two Libyan agents planted a bomb which destroyed the airliner over Scotland, in 1988, killing 270 people.
Libya has incurred U.N. sanctions by rejecting demands that it turn over the two men for trial in the United States or Britain.
